example.detection_method: Detection relies on integration of threat intelligence feeds to flag newly registered domains similar to corporate domains. Email gateway filters analyze SPF/DKIM anomalies, sender reputation, and perform URL sandboxing on embedded links. User education campaigns simulate such spear phishing emails to train CFOs and finance personnel on verifying requests via out-of-band communication channels. SIEM correlation rules alert on wire transfer requests coming from externally originated emails with suspicious domains. Multi-factor verification for wire transfers is enforced, requiring verbal confirmation.

validation.comments: The sample accurately represents a spear phishing scenario targeting a CFO with a fraudulent wire transfer request, aligning well with the problem description. The scenario is realistic, involving domain impersonation, recently registered suspicious domain, and a plausible email content designed to induce urgency. All required fields are present and populated with detailed technical data including email headers, SMTP logs, domain registration info, and indicators that clearly explain why this is a spear phishing attempt. The detection methods and MITRE techniques referenced are appropriate and comprehensive. To improve, the sample could include explicit mention of user education outcomes or examples of verification failures to further illustrate risk reduction effectiveness, but overall it is complete and well-constructed.
